text:
On a whim my wife and I decided to give this place a try, it was around 7:30pm on a a Thursday. When we arrived we notice the menu looked decent but we thought giving the buffet a try would be the best way to gain a sense of the big picture this place had to offer. The smells were amazing and we had a lot of anticipation. Overall the restaurant was clean but at this point that is the best I could say. The buffet had a fair selection of items, however each offering was very slim and it seemed as though this was the left overs of a buffet well over. There was very little rice and many of the other dishes consisted primarily of sauce. It was obvious the last few pieces of tandoori chicken had been there a while. I will say that while the buffet was ill managed you could tell that there was some quality to the food, I could only imagine what it would have tasted fresh. I do understand there is a drop in quality when engaging in a buffet but my harshness is derived from the fact that it was not managed and there seemed to be very little effort to keep the buffet at least a little fresh for new customers. After all they would still be open for a while longer and I don't feel it was time to wind things down buffet wise. 

In addition the server was friendly but our waters were never re-filled and we were never offered more naan.  At least the garlic naan was delicious! This did give us hope that menu items would have much more to offer. 

Overall I think there is a lot of potential. I think there will be a time when we go back to try the menu offerings. I did get the feeling the food could be quite good, so at some point they will get a second chance. I would suggest giving the buffet a walk before deciding to order it.

I honestly would give this place a generous 2 and a half stars if I could just on the hunch there is more potential and my error to choose the buffet was my own mistake. All things considered don't offer up the buffet if you are not ready to have it represent your restaurant in at least some way!

The number of options for Indian food in south Edmonton is always growing; give this place a try and judge for yourself I may have just caught an off day.

First time here, ordered fish appetizer and curry lamb, so delicious both the curry source and the lamb, fish came later, it is as good as the lamb, fresh and tasty...  I wanted to tried variety of num, I did not belive I got them... I felt guilty not able to fish them all, but I had a good experience here and I will come back for sure

Really delicious dinner buffet. Price was good. Selection was good. 

Bads: service seemed a little confused as to what they should do. All of the dishes were a bit spicy (I like spicy, but there was nothing that didn't have some amount of spicyness.)

Goods: the naan was absolutely perfect -- and it kept on coming. I really enjoyed every single dish. I was so full at the end.

This place is an absolute hidden gem. Amazing Indian food... BUFFET STYLE! Now, I don't eat a lot of Indian food, so I stuck with the Butter Chicken. It was perfect and I ate way too much of it. My partner ate far more of a variety and moaned most of the way through his meal in taste bud bliss.

When we were finally done, and debating who would roll the other one out the door, we stopped to looked at their selection of sweets. We'd never had any before, so the gentleman offered us several samples. We fell in love with the milk cake and he boxed up a number of pieces for us to enjoy at home. 

This was a tastefully decorated place, nothing really fancy, just a nice place to eat. The price was unbelievably low for a buffet, only $14.00 per person. I had to ask him if he was charging for both of us. 

I would really recommend this place for anyone who enjoys Indian food (they also deliver).  Based on this experience, I'm thinking my partner and I will become regulars!
Good service and food is pretty good! Prices are not bad. Would recommend this place !

Walked in on a recommendation from co worker. 

I'm no indian food expert but I do like my butter chicken!

Not busy we I arrived for lunch.

Food was fresh and tastey! Friendly space and staff

I would return!

Give them a try!

When we first walked in, it was pretty empty, which made us think why did we even bother making resos but within 10 minutes of our arrival lots of people started showing up. That made us feel confident that this was a good pick for dinner with my family for my bday that night. The decor was very modern and the location is perfect! A wide variety of food to choose from the buffet and it all tasted amazing. For dessert I wanted fresh jalebi (as opposed to the ones sitting in the buffet) and the manager was very accommodating. He was great and always making sure the patrons were taken care of, they seemed short staffed but the manager more than made up for it. The chai masala was a disappointment, definitely was not a good blend of spices. The prices were a bit steep as well, we had a gift card but still had to pay quite a bit out of pocket. But overall it was a great experience and we would go back again!

Came here for dinner and we loved it! The food was very very good (and we have been to India). The prices were good, the service was fast. The waiter was young but very sweet, and when we said we wanted something that was not on the menu he said 'oh I will make it for you'. I know we will be back and I'm happy to have found it.

Just tried this place today for lunch, and it was pretty good. It's nicely decorated inside and the people are nice. The food is really good, although there's not quite as much selection as some places, at least in the buffet. It was also quite expensive for a lunch buffet. We were too full to try any sweets, but they certainly looked good! We will try it again and order from the menu next time.

Quite small. And the staffs were not professional.  They seem to like to enjoy their own time there than do their jobs. When my kids and I went, there was "mini and Mikey mouse " in the place. But they were not there to play with kids. They were busy getting their pictures taking WITHOUT kids. I was not impressed. Although the workers were not teenagers... they sure acted like teenagers who are too busy with their own life.
One question, why do you have a large pole sticking out of the ground right at the end of the slide? That doesn't make any sense?

I came here 2 years ago and had a terrible experience. I got invited back to try it again and was eager since they apparently changed management.
It is definitely not for everyone. We went in on family day and it was pandemonium. Kids everywhere, running, screaming, out of control. My kids were in heaven. They ran through the giant play structure, shot the foam Ball guns, drove the little wheels carts and bounced in the bouncy castle. By the time we left after about an hour and a half they fell asleep.immediately in the car.
Last time I was there it was dirty, this time despite it being crazy busy it was surprisingly well tended.
I will definitely be back with my kids because they had a great time and it's worth it for them to have fun for me to put up with the other parents for a little while

I have so many good things to say about this place, I'll start by saying my then 5 month old daughter was accompanied by an almost 1 year old and a 3 year old along with the families. Just to put across how fun this place was we stayed for SIX hours and there was no tears!
 
This indoor play place is incredible, it has a bouncy castle, a "air gun" shooting area with foam balls, a small kids basketball "court" a huge play structure complete with a few slides, tubes, rock wall, climbing apparatuses, and suspended bridges all safely a few feet in the air. It also includes a baby zone that has a small slide, a ball pit, a few bouncers and lots of cushy mats and fun areas to crawl and climb all safely done in its own zone that is specific to babies (how great is that!) The prices are great all under 12$ for different ages and under a year plays free. 

For the more pricey items it's definitely the food and the arcade, there is no outside food allowed although I didn't see any policing of that rule but there is a concession with your regular gas station sandwiches and salads and the not so kid friendly hamburgers, hot dogs, chicken fingers. They did have lots of drink options but they were way to stocked up on candy and chips and chocolate for my liking. It would've have been nice for the quality of food to match the price but like any outing you kind of know what your getting into! The staff was incredibly nice and accommodation, it was completely breast feeding friendly no one was asked to move or anything. There are change tables and something I really appreciated was the adults were free to play anywhere. Yes that's right, they could play on anything with the kids!


These guys also hold birthday parties, and do have private rooms available. All in all it was really fun! I think though I might stash my own fruits and veggies.

Hell on Earth for the childless among us, myself included. 

Went for a one year old's birthday party on a Saturday afternoon and as soon as I walked into the place my throat tightened up and I wanted to turn around and run away. There's no way that place was meeting fire code capacity. There were kids EVERYWHERE, on the ground, in the sky on giant play structures. Of course there are kids, you say. But there were just too many in there for it to seem safe. Most of the parents looked miserable. Lots of bitchy looking moms and, unsurprisingly, not a lot of dads. 

Can't comment on the price because it's free for adults. There were different price ranges depending on the age of the child you're paying for. Seemed expensive and weird to charge different prices for different sizes of kids.

There was pizza and hot dogs at the party I was at. Pizza was meh, what you would expect. Hot dogs are hot dogs and they were sort of small. Kid sized, I suppose. There was a concession where you could buy food but I heard from relatives it was super expensive. Like, $6 for a tiny personal sized plastic box of veggies.

I guess my cousin had the room rented for a certain amount of time, and the second that time was up we had to be out. It seemed liked my cousin was doing most of the cleaning up and the teens who worked there were just standing around looking bored. 

I understand the need for kids to let out energy and play when the weather is bad outside, but this place was too hectic for any adult to stay sane. I spent less than an hour and won't make the same mistake again!

First time here. Arranged a play date for my 7 and 5 year old. Was suggested by one of the Mom's. Big indoor playground we came early at 9:30. Nobody but 5 kids until about 11:00 am then it became audibly increased in noise. Even with the noise there was still of lots of space for the kids to run and play. They have one big structure with slides, climbing structure and a small arcade area. They had one bouncy castle set up.  They have a little area with these rideable animals that seemed to be a big hit. There is an area with air ball guns and ball pit. They have a toddler area which has a slide and a ball pit. They do have a cafe with a big selection of fresh fruit, sandwich and snacks. Reasonable price. If you want to book a party they have 3 rooms available. Look online to book. They also offer parent date night mostly every Friday from 5 - 8:30, coat $30 per child and each additional sibling is 1/2 price. Something to keep in mind in the future. They also offer in and out privileges so we went out for lunch and came back around 3 pm. Definitely more busy at 3 pm as several parties were going on.  For the mom's out there it was nice to sit and talk and socialize while the kids played. So that was a bonus.  Wound recommend this indoor playground.

Me and my family will not be returning to the tree house very dissapointed 30 some dollars for two kids to get in plus 30 dollars for lunch unbelievable my 8 year old didn't enjoy himself it is aimed mostly for 6 and under I would say 4.75 for a cupcake is insane . Tons of bully moms there and mean kids terrible experience manager refused to help with situation my 4 year old daughter left with a bruise on her cheek because someone's child hit her in the face when she didn't get her way!


If I could give this place no stars I would

I am so unimpressed what a waste of money

Treehouse indoor playground is like a mixture between chucky cheese and a mcdonalds play place, except they charge $10 to get a 2 year old in.
Treehouse is a mess, I did not see a single adult staff member the entire time I was there. The washrooms were disgusting; you have to go in with sock feet and I literally threw my socks in the garbage afterwards because I came out of the bathroom with sticky feet.... Gross
The games area had 9 broken down machines with out of order signs on them. When I asked one of the staff about it he said 'we are waiting for a repair man, it's a little ridiculous'.... He took the words out if my mouth. 
I asked to speak to the manager before I left and was told that he was 'upstairs'. The kid at the counter called 'John' the manager and relayed my concerns, then when he hung up I asked if he was coming down and was told that if I wanted to speak to him in person he could call him back... Don't worry John, I was in a rush to get out of there. Hopefully when you guys close on February 3rd for a whole day of cleaning, you also take the time to do some staff training and fix your games machines.
Don't waste your money taking your kids here, there are plenty of other good, safe, clean options around because treehouse is none of those things.

I've come here a few times with my children and every time there are children running around the play structures with no socks on. The staff have never approached any children to put their socks on and usually the socks are just randomly tossed in a corner of the play structure. We are always asked when we enter if everyone in our group has socks on. Why ask if you don't plan to enforce your own policy?  The entire place seems dirty at any time we have come which is funny because it seems like they are closed a lot for cleaning. We always get the game tokens which is starting not to make sense since half of the games are out of order.  The food is horribly overpriced and tastes like garbage. Save your money.

This was my first time going to this Indoor Playground as my daughter (who is currently 6 months) was invited to a birthday party for a friends daughter. I researched the location before going because I had never heard of or seen this place before; one big thing is don't forget to wear socks or you cannot enter. You have to leave your shoes at the door (anyone ever have that fear that they'll be shoeless by the time they leave?) If you're an adult, you're admission is free, but obviously you must have a child with you or be attending one of the many parties they throw in different rooms. Not sure how much different aged children cost, as my daughter was allowed in for free (I think anyone under 12 months is free)....

Our friend had booked a room to have the party in; nothing but tiny chairs for tiny bums and a tiny table for tiny legs/knees so parents/adults be prepared to stand, sit on the ground or pray to whatever god you believe in that your bum doesn't break that tiny chair.... (Or borrow one from the seating area outside if you can, however there is not much space in the room....)

Their is a little area for the more little ones (toddler and baby) which was nice to see because my little girl absolutely loved the rocking animal (or was it a bug?) and was uncertain but seemed to enjoy the ball pit and slide. (FYI; you may or may not be able to fit down the tiny slide but you are definitely not permitted in the ball pit as noted by a sign...lol)

They did have a "Minnie Mouse" mascot to surprise the birthday girl, as she is a huge fan of Minnie. From a child's perspective, probably cute and seems legit, but from an adults perspective it seemed as though they purchased the costume off of the cheapest internet site ever. The costume was faded, pilled and you could definitely see that it was a human under that big head from a child's line of view. The mascot stayed maybe 5 minutes than went about her merry way, they had to bring her back in to actually take some photos with the birthday girl and other children.

If you don't have children, but have to attend an event here or bring a niece/nephew, be prepared for child anarchy; children ran amok screaming, crying and there were quite a few parents that seemed more interested in their phones than little Susie or Bobby screaming at them to "watch me!" "watch me!"....

It's awesome that they have an indoor playground for children to get exercise as with socialize with other children during those chilly or cold months, but the place itself seems very cheap yet gouging everyone for money when it comes to food or drink. I might be back as baby get's older, not certain however.... I will however, never book a party room here; WAY too expensive for the size of it, how long you can stay in it and what they offer as "perks" yet you have to clean up the room when you're done (put away chairs, clean the tables, etc.) & the minute your time is up, someone is there to usher you out of it (I assume they book back-to-back)....
Friendly staff and lots to keep kids entertained
I like this treehouse the owners update the play area and added a few new arcade games. Family friendly of course and clean. Staff is visible and ready to help if something comes up.

I thought this place was great. Very clean and comparative prices to the other playgrounds in the city. My child loves the play equipment and ball pit area (he's three). The staff maybe aren't as friendly as they could be, but I'm really not there for them to serve me. I really enjoy this place and will be returning

My toddler loves it here. Lots to do, pretty clean considering it's a kids play park, and the price is pretty good. Great place to go on your own or with a group. Lots of tables and lockers, bathrooms are really clean and the food is pretty good.

It's our go to a rainy or super cold day.

For the parents out there, you know that throwing a kids birthday party can be a traumatic and harrowing experience.  Everything from the planning, to the hosting, to clean up can lead to draining a few bottles of wine or crushing a flat of beer quicker than you can say "Timmy don't put that in your nose!!!".

My kid just turned 3, and to be honest, I was dreading the prospect of having to throw another birthday for the little guy.  Love him, but the ol' spare tire can't handle any more beer. 

I'm happy to say that having his birthday at The Treehouse was a great idea.  They made the whole process quick, easy and painless.  We literally walked in, made sure the date that we wanted was free, booked a room for an hour, and picked a package (various options that include admission for kids, food, and themed party including a visit from a good selection of different mascots). They even have online cards that you can cusromize and print out! The host there was super helpful in making suggestions as well.

We had the kids and parents arrive an hour beforehand to give the kids some time to play, went up to the party room for an hour to have lunch and cake, and then back down for more play time. 

The facility is clean, the jungle gym was very impressive, ball cannon was a blast, with lots of engaging fun for kids from toddler age and up. Even the dad's had fun playing a friendly game of hoops that may or may not have led to a little name calling and shaming in front of their respective toddlers. 

I have to say I like this place a lot more than Chuck-e-Cheeses.  There is a small area that is token-driven, with the majority of the space dominated by the jungle gym and toddler areas. They also have free lockers that were a really nice touch. 

Once we were all done, we settled our bill, grabbed our stuff, and left. No clean up, no worries about pesky lingerers who just won't get out of your house.  Expect to have your ear drums blown out by the hordes of screaming kids but I'd say that's par for the course when it comes to these things.

Love this place! But only during the week, weekends are hell on earth in there. 
My son is 2, I work around the corner, we go on Tuesdays and Thursdays and play all evening! He has a blast because he isnt confined to the toddler area. On tuesdays and thursdays its not busy and my son is able to climb all over the place without getting pushed and pulled by a million kids.  Perfect way to spend a evening playing when it gets cold outside
Great place for kids to run around look forward  to my son's birthday here :)$ 12 for kids is good deal for cold winter fun. And love parents night off!

My little one is only 10.5 months old right now, so when invited to places like this I am very hesitant as I'm not sure what age rage of children will be there. I decided to give it a try because a girlfriend of mine was taking her two little ones here. I checked the website and saw that because mine is under one, she would be free (AWESOME!). So we went. 

The staff was friendly and prompt when trying to enter. Once inside you see the HUGE Jungle gym area, a bouncy castle, a games area and a toddlers area. I brought my babe into the toddler area to play. The first part wasn't bad. There's lots of toys and space to play. The only thing that had me worried was that a lot of parents didn't follow the rules about height going into the ball pit. There were a few that went into the ball pit and were acting a little crazy when the little toddlers were in there. Scaring a few and stepped on my friends daughter. I would suggest more staff to do rounds and keep an eye out for bigger kids in the toddler area. 

If you want coffee, a drink, or food there is concession available as well. They have a wide variety of foods including healthy snacks for your kids.

The only thing I don't really understand, is when you leave you have to show your stamp that you receive when you come in... not sure the point of that, but I had to wait a few minutes for the staff to finish with people waiting to get in.

Everything seemed clean and taken care of. And definitely could see me bringing my little one here as she grows to burn off steam in the winter time.

This is the loudest, craziest busiest place you'll ever go. There are kids and parents jammed into an area overflowing with slides, jungle gym, cafe, baby area, bouncy castle, arcade and birthday rooms. 

It heaven for kids though. I bring my kids here and I won't see them for an hour. Once again hadn't seen my son in so long I had the page him at the front desk because I was a little worried. 

Don't fear though! They do the same number stamp as Chucky Cheese so no one can make off with your babies. You and your child's numbers have to match for you to leave the play area. 

I bring my crochet or iPhone and headphones and zone out. It's actually quite relaxing. 


The food is good but as expensive as you'd expect.
Such a lovely play area, it's a locally owned business. Kept really clean it's for the younger ages as it's smaller than the other indoor play areas. Support local they are closed of a Tuesday.

I hate to put attention to this Winners because I swear no one knows its here and I want my sizes too still be available but it is my duty as a yelper to review. They always have inventory that fits, not the kind where you say yeah its kind of loose but will do. There is more than enough staff there to meet customer expectations. I even think they have a full time person at the change room cause every time I went there, someone was there. The house ware dept has plenty of unique and affordable merchandise. I usually end up buying a few pairs of shoes here a year, they're cheap and actually have stock on size 13. The best part is show up after 7 and the store is emmmmmmpty because all the seniors in the area are back home and getting ready for bed. Senior population is high in this area. So come check it out but leave the size 33 pants alone, size 13 shoes off limits and leave the large v necks alone but all else is availabe.

Came in yesterday for some deals to find, and I did. I scored big on the clearance rack . I got 3 very nice skirts for the office, all lined and designer made. For $3.00 pr skirt.. Now that's a deal.. Also got a winter sweater for $5.00. They have some great shoes, and bags. Came in at about 3:30 pm and it wasn't busy at all. Compared to some of the other Winners were you have to fight the crowds..

This one is meh, it's messy, has a poor selection compared to other locations and seems to carry a lot of damaged stuff. Not one of their better stores. On the plus side, the staff is very friendly and helpful.

It's not the biggest store and it seems to have gone through so many changes over the years. They used to have a huge and constantly changing variety of goods but they have trimmed down. 
They've added jewelry which is nice but it seems like old styles as do most things here. Last years' leftovers. There's a smaller housewares section, but still good things for the kitchen. Not much for furniture or decor anymore. I used to get all my scrap booking supplies here but they no longer carry this type of merchandise.  I buy candles, small blankets and pillows here but the selection isn't as impressive. I loved the brand names at good prices but don't find as many great brands.
I can still find clothing deals, shoes, makeup and hair goodies. The current vibe of the store is more like a clearance wearhouse. 
I don't think Capilano is a great location for Winners. It's more of a Walmart & Dollarama neighbourhood unfortunately. I understand their challenges in finding what sells well here.
They have a clothing clearance section that's well stocked but you need to check the clothing for damage carefully. 
The store is clean and organized but definitely less to choose from. I still go just because I want to, but more than 75% of the time I leave empty handed.

Dropped in to this Winners location more on a whim as I was in the area.

Parking is fairly decent; tons of space.

Once thing I really liked about this location is the spaciousness, organization and brightness of the store. I didn't get the opportunity to engage with an employee as they didn't really have anything that caught my eye on this trip & didn't need any assistance.

As I browsed, I found a good majority of their items were priced fairly steep; not certain if this is the thing with all Winners now, but they seem to carry more "brand name" items that are high priced (maybe discounted $10 off the original)....

I might be back in a blue moon.

This may be the smallest and most poorly stocked Winners store in all of Edmonton, but  
I still find tons of beauty supplies to fit my needs.
From Moroccan hair oil to fancy French milled soaps to high end designer eye shadows. 
I refuse to pay the original retail sticker price for anything. 
The store is usually pretty lonely with few customers.  This gives me plenty of time to quietly browse and try things on without feeling rushed.   There is no line up for check out.  Just me. 
I feel like I've gotten a real bargain after walking out with a huge bag of girly stuff.

After all of the renovations going on in the Capilano mall area, I expected Winners to undergo a transformation as well. But not too much had changed apart from the look of the store. 

The store is always messy but in an organized chaos kind of way, especially in shoes and housewares. Part of the fun of shopping at Winners though is hunting through all the mundane stuff to find something awesome. 

I feel like they used to have a lot more clearance items available. There's still a decent amount of cheap things to buy however! Sometimes the discount clothes are super grungy and have loose threads, etc but it's usually fixable stuff.

Awesome POSSUM over the moon kool kat park!

This spray park is WICKED!  There are so many features including toddler and big kid areas that I cannot imagine anyone getting bored here!

I uploaded lots of pics, so be sure to take a peek!

This spray park is surrounded by numerous other playground features and an unfenced lake so I do recommend a 1:1 ration of adults to young children if there is a chance they could wander off to the lake and get in trouble.

There are indoor washrooms for getting changed but no concessions here full-time though you are likely to see an ice cream truck on a hot day.

On the day we visited, there was a green shack staff member playing in the water area but this spray park is not otherwise staffed during all open hours.

If you haven't yet visited this pray park with your kiddos, it is worth the drive regardless of where you live in the city!

Here almost every weekend - has 4 great places for kids to play and even close to washrooms with change tables and wheelchair accessible in the baby park, family friendly of course. There is a dog park and golf course but I haven't gone in those areas yet. New addition to park telus has set up a solar wifi charge station bench just bring a charge cord for your phone!

We thoroughly enjoy this off leash area. There is open area and a walk along the ravine stream. Dogs are often found cavorting in the water. Tree coverage keeps that area cool in the summer and it smells fabulous. It borders a golf coarse so you know it is green. We have been going for several years and recommend that park to anyone and everyone.

Here almost every weekend - has 4 great places for kids to play and even close to washrooms with change tables and wheelchair accessible in the baby park, family friendly of course. There is a dog park and golf course but I haven't gone in those areas yet.
The best park in Edmonton for kids!! Picnic sites, a pond, huge rock climbing, two large playgrounds and a huge splash park. I will drive far for this park anyday.

This park is OUT OF THIS WORLD!

There are so many playgrounds here, it is easy for me to get lost! 

TONS of parking, at least 5 separate playgrounds including - toddler playground, big kid playground, rock wall/climbing and rope course play ground, HUGE spray park, and a freaking monkey bars playground... that's right, I said a monkey bars playground with more than 20 different types/styles of monkey bars.

This park is INSANE - if you haven't been here, you NEED to come.  Get up, right now and go!

So pray tell, why am I only giving 4 stars rather than 5 stars?  Well... Okay, compared to my family's personal have spray park, this park does not offer concessions, is not staffed during all open hours, and has a lake that little ones could run off to quickly and possibly get wet or be in a dangerous situation.

So... If coming here with only big kids that you trust not to go in the lake or run out in the parking lot, then this park may become your very favourite.  If you are like me with two kids under 6, this park requires a 1:1 ratio of adults to children to be certain of safety.

I will most definitely be coming back here again and again and again!

Note: this is specifically a review of the off leash dog park at the Jackie Parker recreation area.

We really love this off leash area. The people and dogs are always very friendly. We find ourselves there at least a few times a week and have gotten to know many regulars.

Our favourite part of Jackie Parker is the forest walking trail that outlines the perimeter of the park. My dog loves to explore in the trees and it's a good place to get out of the wind or sun. It's a pretty short walk, taking about 15 minutes from one end to the other. It's a relaxed stroll with only one stretch that can be a bit dicey in the winter (see photo). This path also feels nature-y without being more than a few steps from the action in the field. This is especially important walking alone with a not so protective dog. I've always felt very safe at Jackie Parker (which is not something I can say about every place I've walked my pup).

There are a number of benches and garbage cans strategically placed around the park. And for the most part people are good about picking up after their pets. It's usually busy enough that there are dogs to interact with but not so crazy you can't find parking.

I was also charmed by Jackie Parker when we visited in December and found many of the trees along the forest path had been decorated for Christmas. Let's just say it was pretty magical!

Amazing park to be with your kids in every age. 
The spray park is amazing. Big and lots variety of stay works. This park will keep your little monsters busy all day long!! Kids can have a blast at the spray park or the rock climbing park or the giant play park with so many different kinds of things that kids can play on. My kids just loved the every part of everything here. The rock-climbing area, the variety of monkey bars and  of course the spray park that makes loud wild animal sounds.  Kids find the place so excited and fun that they don't get wander off to a feild or get lost. They stay within those 3 parks that can provide them with all their needs for fun. 
I liked how they had the toddler's park separated from the big Kids' park. Felt much safe and free for the little one to play in the park. 

You do need to be aware that there are quite of bit of ants and lot much shade around spray park where kids most likely to be at. Also, since it's a public place.. and full of kids and all different kinds of kids, parents should be aware of other kids whom we might call 'troubles' . I have noticed that there are always few kids who have problem with sharing toys/equipments/ spots. Can be kids who hit others or bite.. so.. 
I just want to say that ***it is important for the parents to just know where your kids are and how they are behaving around others. And clean up after yourselves and the kids.***

Overall,  I love this place, kids love it. We have been going back almost every second days and have a blast every time we go. Love love love it!!

I've stopped here several times over the years when my body needs a break from being in the vehicle. Tonight I sat way too long in the lineup at Peter's, so naturally I thought of this location on my way home. 

It was super windy and quite chilly tonight. I debated just looking at the lake from the vehicle but I wanted to see what birds were out there. So I had a fast eating kind of picnic while watching the geese at the lake, checked out the playground to see if it's worth bringing the nephews and nieces (definitely cool!) and just enjoyed watching the sun set from different angles. It's a large park with the road dividing the off leash area from where the playground is. Trees look to be the boundary to the gold course further back in the park. 

If you're looking for well set up group spaces for picnics that are family friendly, I'd recommend this location. Lots of parking too. Oh
Nice area with lots of stuff for the Children but not many Washrooms even the toilets didn't seem that Clean wish they had a Porter when the Park gets busy

Parking can be insane. Minus 10 stars for parking.  Even though there are lots of spaces, it's always packed.  I don't actually think they should add more because that would add more to the crowds.

Aside from that.. 
Great playground and water park. 
Accessible for our kiddo in his wheelchair. 
Rentable sites. 
Skating in the winter with an inside space to lace up in. 
Real bathroom. 

Love this place!

Just want to get this out there, this park is THE BEST park for any summer activities. Personally, I have so many memories from this park ever since it opened.

They have so many cool things to do at this park. It's not a simple park first and foremost. This park includes a playground, a spray park, and a giant pond. They have a BBQ and firepit station, which is beneficial if anyone wants to do a picnic or just gathering around the campfire. There's lots of space to run around, there's parking, and across from the park, you can just grab a coffee since there is a Tim Hortons. The location is everything, and includes parking!  

Honestly, this place is just a beauty and if you are just looking to get out during the winter or summer, it is worth it. Totally recommend!

Jackie Parker Recreation Area is a great big area with many amenities for the family.  There are picnic sites, a spray park, climbing wall, playground, small lake (skating pond in winter), walking trails, fire pit, and an off-leash area.  The Millwoods golf-course is also very close by.

I am going to focus my review on the off-leash area as the only kids I have are of the furry four-legged kind.  So we go out to Jackie Parker quite a bit with the dogs.  Our other favourite off-leash area is Terwillegar but Jackie Parker is becoming a new favourite.

The off-leash are is quite large and expansive and has a kind of a figure-8 walking trail.  There are poopy bag dispensers on location and as per usual people leave extra bags out as well.  There is a notice board for community info as well as lost/found posts etc.  The last time I was there they have also installed a Little Free Library box.

The parking lot is a bit small in the off-leash area to accommodate the number of people that use this area (-1 star), but you can always park in the playground parking lot and walk across the road to enter the off-leash area.  Be respectful though as the playground area is not off-leash so you should keep your dogs on leash until you reach the off-leash area (not everyone likes dogs, or is unfired of them no matter how gentle).
